description: TrendLens is an interactive environmental investigation platform that uses NASA Earth science data to help people explore long-term temperature trends across different regions of the world.
summary:
TrendLens is an interactive environmental investigation platform that uses NASA Earth science data to help people explore long-term temperature trends across different regions of the world.

Users can compare locations, investigate historical temperature patterns, examine month-by-month changes, and explore statistical evidence through an interactive global map and scientific dashboard.
details:
Data and methodology

TrendLens uses monthly near-surface air temperature (T2M) data from NASA POWER for 1981–2025. The meteorological data is derived from the MERRA-2 reanalysis.

Monthly observations are validated, missing-value sentinels are excluded, and annual means are calculated from valid monthly records.

Theil–Sen slope is used to estimate robust trend magnitude, while the Mann–Kendall test evaluates evidence of a monotonic trend. The dashboard also presents OLS regression as a complementary trend estimate.

The Global Explorer uses location coordinates obtained through Open-Meteo geocoding and retrieves NASA POWER data for the selected point.

What makes TrendLens different?

Rather than presenting a single global temperature number, TrendLens allows users to investigate individual locations, compare regional patterns, and explore the seasonal structure of historical temperature changes.

Its emphasis is on transparent methods, reproducible calculations, and communicating scientific uncertainty.

Limitations

TrendLens currently investigates selected geographic points; it does not provide a complete global temperature raster or forecast future temperatures.

NASA POWER T2M is reanalysis-derived meteorological data, not a direct satellite measurement of surface temperature.

The Mann–Kendall p-values are unadjusted for serial autocorrelation. Seasonal slopes are exploratory estimates and are not separate significance claims. Results should be interpreted with these limitations in mind.

Data sources and acknowledgements

  • NASA POWER: https://power.larc.nasa.gov/
  • NASA POWER documentation: https://power.larc.nasa.gov/docs/
  • Open-Meteo Geocoding API: https://open-meteo.com/
  • OpenStreetMap contributors: https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright

Technology

Next.js, TypeScript, React, Recharts, Leaflet, OpenStreetMap, NASA POWER API and Open-Meteo Geocoding API.

Generative AI tools assisted with software development and implementation. Scientific calculations are performed by the application's implemented statistical functions using retrieved data.
